1                        I.    WITNESS IDENTIFICATION

2    Q.   Please state your name and business address.

3    A.   My name is Allison M. Johnson. My business address is 3500 Blake Street, Denver,

4         Colorado 80205.

5    Q.   On whose behalf are you testifying in this proceeding?

6    A.   I am filing testimony on behalf of Southwestern Public Service Company, a New

7         Mexico corporation (“SPS”) and wholly-owned electric utility subsidiary of Xcel

8         Energy Inc.

9    Q.   Are you the same Allison M. Johnson who filed direct testimony on behalf of

10        SPS in this case?

11   A.   Yes.

12   Q.   Were Attachments AMJ-STIP-R1 and AMJ-STIP-R2 prepared by you or

13        under your direct supervision and control?

14   A.   Yes.




                                             1
                                    Case No. 25-00079-UT

                                 Comprehensive Stipulation
                                              of
                                     Allison M. Johnson

                         II.   PURPOSE AND SUMMARY OF TESTIMONY

 1   Q.   What is the purpose of your testimony in this phase of the case?

 2   A.   The purpose of my rebuttal testimony is to respond to arguments presented in the

 3        testimony in opposition to stipulation filed by New Mexico Public Regulation

 4        Commission (“Commission”) Utility Division Staff (“Staff”) on July 7, 2026. In

 5        particular, I respond to the testimony of the following Staff witness:

 6               •   Jonah B. Mauldin, who testifies on behalf of Staff

 7   Q.   Please summarize your testimony and overall recommendations.

 8   A.   As stated in my testimony In Support of Stipulation, I recommend that the

 9        Commission approve SPS’s Comprehensive Stipulation (“Stipulation”) as it

10        represents a reasonable compromise among the Signatories. I also refute several of

11        the arguments provided by Staff witness Mauldin, namely his assertion that the

12        stipulated revenue deficiency of $90 million lacks transparency and that a large

13        portion of the settlement balance is undefined. Finally, I address Mr. Mauldin’s

14        concern that the Stipulation does not specify the Excess Liability Insurance (“ELI”)

15        regulatory asset balance and therefore the balance was not adjusted to reflect

16        decreases in actual expense.




                                               2
                                    Case No. 25-00079-UT
                               Rebuttal Testimony in Support of
                                 Comprehensive Stipulation
                                              of
                                     Allison M. Johnson

                   III.   SPS’S REBUTTAL TO STAFF’S OPPOSITION OF THE
                                 STIPULATED REVENUE DEFICIENCY

 1   Q.   What do you discuss in this section of your testimony?

 2   A.   I will summarize the main points of Mr. Mauldin’s testimony and provide clarity

 3        to the aspects of the Stipulation that he states are undefined or lacking transparency.

 4   Q.   Do you agree with Mr. Mauldin’s assertion that the stipulated revenue

 5        deficiency is undefined or lacks transparency?

 6   A.   No. Mr. Mauldin argues there are $35.9 million in non-defined reductions that are

 7        not explained by the Stipulation’s express terms and are “black box,” or, not

 8        transparent. He provides a table, JBM-1, in support of these arguments. It contains

 9        three sections, or panels. Panel A reconciles the difference between SPS’s original

10        revenue deficiency of $175,354,544 and its revised deficiency of $167,551,358

11        included in SPS’s Comprehensive List of Revisions filing made on March 20, 2026

12        and Notice of Correction filing made on March 25, 2026. Panel B attempts to

13        reconcile this amount to the stipulated revenue deficiency of $90,000,000, while

14        Panel C reiterates Staff’s proposed adjustments to arrive at their recommended

15        deficiency of $47,691,101.

16               It is Panel B that is problematic. Within the table, it shows that SPS includes

17        a non-defined reduction to the revenue requirement of $35,930,622 to arrive at the


                                                3
                                    Case No. 25-00079-UT
                               Rebuttal Testimony in Support of
                                 Comprehensive Stipulation
                                              of
                                     Allison M. Johnson

 1        $90 million stipulated revenue increase. In the notes to Table JMB-1, it states “Non-

 2        Defined Reductions represent the residual difference between identified stipulation

 3        terms and the stipulated revenue deficiency.” The table lists several known

 4        revisions, such as the reduction to return on equity (“ROE”) and the adjustment to

 5        capital structure, but neglects to include a number of additional adjustments that

 6        were explicitly stated in my testimony in support of the Stipulation. Had these been

 7        included, the non-defined reduction amount would be significantly smaller.

 8   Q.   Can you provide a table that reconciles all of the adjustments made to arrive

 9        at the stipulated revenue deficiency of $90 million?

10   A.   Yes. The table below presents the revenue requirement adjustments in more detail,

11        beginning with the initial filing revenue deficiency of $175,354,544 and arriving at

12        the stipulated revenue increase of $90 million. Please note that the non-defined

13        reduction amount is less than two million dollars, a significantly smaller amount

14        than the $35,930,622 presented by Mr. Mauldin in Table JBM-1.




                                               4
                                    Case No. 25-00079-UT
                               Rebuttal Testimony in Support of
                                 Comprehensive Stipulation
                                              of
                                     Allison M. Johnson

1                                    Table AMJ-STIP-R1

    Adjust Return on Equity to 9.5%                                          ($27,982,137)

    Adjust Legacy Meter Amortization                                            (3,364,391)
    Adjust Capital Structure 54.7% Equity; 45.3% Debt                           (3,283,376)
    Adjust ELI Test Year Expense                                                (2,417,293)
    Adjust Jurisdictional Allocator                                             (1,437,157)
    Property Tax Adjustment (Mar. 20, 2026 Revisions Filing)                      (711,504)
    Remove Return on Solar PTC DTA                                                (525,382)
    Adjust Community Solar Garden O&M                                             (235,602)
    O&M Labor Escalation (Mar. 20, 2026 Revisions Filing)                         (189,228)
    Adjust Rate Case Expenses                                                     (136,150)
    Cunningham BESS Deferred Taxes (Mar. 20, 2026 Revisions Filing)                 321,267
    Adjust NMPRC fees/Uncollectible                                                 461,831
    FERC Account 370 Adjustment (Mar. 20, 2026 Revisions Filing)                  1,464,495
    Solar/BESS O&M (Mar. 20, 2026 Revisions Filing)                               2,376,122
    Non-defined Reductions                                                      (1,962,937)
    Total Reductions                                                         ($85,354,544)
    SPS Stipulated Revenue Deficiency                                          $90,000,000


2   Q.    What are the most significant adjustments that Mr. Mauldin excluded from

3         the reconciliation presented in Panel B of Table JBM-1?

4   A.    There are a number of adjustments that were excluded from Panel B of Table JBM-

5         1. Listed below are the primary adjustments, in order of significance:
                                                5
                                        Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                   Rebuttal Testimony in Support of
                                     Comprehensive Stipulation
                                                  of
                                         Allison M. Johnson

 1        •    the removal of all Battery Energy Storage System (“BESS”) Long-Term

 2             Purchased Power Agreement (“LTPPA”) capacity costs

 3        •    revised depreciation rates

4         •    the removal of the Southwest Power Pool deficiency payment, and

5         •    the removal of cash working capital from rate base

6    Q.       Based on Table AMJ-STIP-R1, is the stipulated revenue deficiency of $90

7             million supported and reasonable?

8    A.       Yes. This table clearly displays the revenue requirement impact of all adjustments

9             necessary for reconciling the initial filed deficiency of $175,354,544 to the

10            stipulated revenue deficiency of $90 million. All of these adjustments are the result

11            of a cost of service that accurately reflects the Future Test Year (“FTY”), expert

12            testimony, and extensive negotiation and compromise to reflect the positions of

13            both SPS and the parties. The fundamental principles of ratemaking were observed

14            and properly flowed through the cost of service model in order to arrive at a

15            reasonable settlement among the Signatories.




                                                   6
                                    Case No. 25-00079-UT
                               Rebuttal Testimony in Support of
                                 Comprehensive Stipulation
                                              of
                                     Allison M. Johnson

 1   Q.   Why does a “non-defined reduction” still exist in order to arrive at the

 2        stipulated revenue deficiency?

 3   A.   As explained in the Testimony in Support of Comprehensive Stipulation of Ms. Zoë

 4        E. Lees, the comprehensive stipulation represents a compromise among the

5         Signatories on a number of contested issues in the rate case proceeding. While the

6         Stipulation explicitly states the issues where the Signatories were able to reach

7         agreement, along with the associated change to the revenue requirement, it does not

 8        attempt to resolve all contested issues within the case. The non-defined reduction

 9        of under $2 million dollars represents the remaining reduction required to arrive at

10        the stipulated revenue increase of $90 million and isn’t specifically tied to any

11        issue. This is normal practice in previous comprehensive settlements. This $2

12        million dollar settlement adjustment is a significantly smaller reduction in

13        comparison to the $35.9 million amount shown in Table JMB-1 of Mr. Mauldin’s

14        testimony. Finally, the immaterial magnitude of the non-defined reduction as

15        compared to the stipulated revenue deficiency indicates the results of the settlement

16        negotiations are reasonable.




                                               7
                                    Case No. 25-00079-UT
                               Rebuttal Testimony in Support of
                                 Comprehensive Stipulation
                                              of
                                     Allison M. Johnson

 1   Q.   Have all of the adjustments to the revenue requirement been thoroughly

 2        discussed in prior testimony?

 3   A.   Yes. All of the adjustments in the table have been discussed in either SPS’s

 4        Comprehensive List of Revisions, filed March 20, 2026, or my testimony in support

 5        of Comprehensive Stipulation, filed June 30, 2026. In addition, SPS filed updated

 6        schedules on July 2, 2026, in response to Bench Request 3 of the Hearing

 7        Examiners, which supports in detail the stipulated revenue requirement as it relates

 8        to rate base, capital structure, and the income statement.

 9   Q.   Would it be possible for Staff or other parties to independently arrive at the

10        amounts shown in Table AMJ-STIP-R1?

11   A.   Yes. Staff or other parties could utilize the SPS NM Test Year Cost of Service

12        Model.xlsx, located in Attachment AMJ-12 in my direct testimony, to arrive at the

13        adjustment amounts in the table. However, due to the dynamic nature of the case,

14        in which we have made changes to multiple aspects of the cost of service, such as

15        jurisdictional allocators, ROE, capital structure and labor escalators, the

16        incremental changes calculated by this model may not exactly tie to the amounts in

17        the table.   Order of operations would need to be kept the same, and some

18        adjustments will be slightly different than the amounts in the table. Mr. Mauldin
                                                8
                             Case No. 25-00079-UT
                        Rebuttal Testimony in Support of
                          Comprehensive Stipulation
                                       of
                              Allison M. Johnson

1   noted this in his JMB-1 table, which contained a rounding variance of $1,943 and

2   the associated note: “In Panel C, the $1,943 rounding variance reflects minor

3   differences arising from adjustment interactions in the cost-of-service model.”




                                         9
                                    Case No. 25-00079-UT
                               Rebuttal Testimony in Support of
                                 Comprehensive Stipulation
                                              of
                                     Allison M. Johnson

 1   Q.   Are you providing any attachments with your testimony?

 2   A.   Yes. I am providing a live cost of service model that reflects the Stipulation as

 3        Attachment AMJ-STIP-R1 SPS NM Test Year Cost of Service Model.xlsx.

 4        Additionally, Attachment AMJ-STIP-R2 contains electronic workpapers which

 5        support all of the adjustments made to the cost of service to arrive at the $90 million

 6        stipulated revenue deficiency. Both attachments are similar to the aforementioned

 7        AMJ-12 attachment included in my direct testimony.

 8   Q.   How does Table AMJ-STIP-R1 compare to Table AMJ-STIP-1, provided in

 9        your testimony in support of Stipulation?

10   A.   The two tables are intended to illustrate different aspects of the settlement and

11        therefore rely on different comparison points. Table AMJ-STIP-1 shows the

12        progression from the revenue requirement established in Case No. 22-00286-UT to

13        the stipulated revenue increase of $90 million. By contrast, Table AMJ-STIP-R1

14        begins with SPS’s initial revenue requirement request in this proceeding and

15        reconciles that request to the stipulated settlement amount. Together, the tables

16        provide complementary views of the adjustments that resulted in the negotiated

17        resolution.


                                                10
                                    Case No. 25-00079-UT
                               Rebuttal Testimony in Support of
                                 Comprehensive Stipulation
                                              of
                                     Allison M. Johnson

                            IV.    ELI REGULATORY ASSET BALANCE

 1   Q.   What do you discuss in this section of your testimony?

 2   A.   In this section of my testimony, I discuss Staff’s position regarding the ELI

 3        regulatory asset balance. Mr. Mauldin supports SPS’s withdrawal of the ELI

 4        expense tracker but argues that the Stipulation does not go far enough on the

 5        deferred ELI regulatory asset. Specifically, I address Mr. Mauldin’s statement that

 6        the Stipulation does not specify the regulatory asset balance.

 7   Q.   On Page 11, Lines 17-18 of Mr. Mauldin’s Testimony in Opposition to

 8        Stipulation he states, “The Stipulation does not address the regulatory asset

 9        balance, therefore Staff is under the assumption the balance will be set at

10        SPS’s requested amount.” Is this assumption accurate?

11   A.   No. In Mr. Mauldin’s direct testimony he recommended that SPS update the ELI

12        regulatory asset balance based on updated information SPS provided in response

13        to Staff Interrogatory No. 2-6(a). SPS agreed that the roll forward provided in

14        response to Staff Interrogatory No. 2-6(a) includes data based on actual amounts

15        recorded in SPS’s accounting records versus an estimate of the regulatory asset

16        balance that was the best available data at the time of

17        SPS’s initial filing. Although the regulatory asset balance was not specifically


                                               11
                              Case No. 25-00079-UT
                         Rebuttal Testimony in Support of
                           Comprehensive Stipulation
                                        of
                               Allison M. Johnson

1   stated in the terms of the Stipulation, SPS did update the regulatory asset balance

2   to $26,233,655 based on the forecasted November 2026 ending balance provided

3   in SPS’s response to Staff Interrogatory No. 2-6(a) within the cost of service that

4   reflects the stipulated revenue deficiency. This adjustment can be found in the

5   supporting workpapers provided in Attachment AMJ-STIP-R2.




                                         12
                                   Case No. 25-00079-UT
                              Rebuttal Testimony in Support of
                                Comprehensive Stipulation
                                             of
                                    Allison M. Johnson

                                      V.   RECOMMENDATION

 1   Q.   Do you have any concluding remarks?

 2   A.   Yes.   I recommend that the Commission approve the Stipulation without

3         modification for the reasons described previously in my testimony. The revenue

 4        increase of $90 million embodied in the Stipulation is the product of extensive

 5        negotiations among the Signatories and reflects concrete, numerically identifiable

 6        adjustments that collectively result in a reasonable and carefully considered

 7        determination of the Company’s cost of service.

 8   Q.   Does this conclude your pre-filed rebuttal testimony in support of the

 9        Stipulation?

10   A.   Yes.
